title: Inference workshop field notes — long-context & serving ideas
body:
Quick context / what's this file:
These are my raw field notes from the small workshop on long-context serving patterns (9/14). Mostly a brain-dump: paper skims, sketches for experiments, implementation tradeoffs, and TODOs to sync with SRE and runtime. Keep informal — will refine into an RFC if any of these lines up with roadmap.

Top-level themes I care about
- Efficient KV caching: sharding, eviction, and cross-request reuse when context spans thousands of tokens.
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs: small increases in per-request latency can yield large token-cost wins via batching/caching.
- Graceful fallback: how to piggyback model-variant fallback decisions on cache miss patterns.
- Practical evals: light-weight probes that measure semantic degradation (not just perplexity) when using partial caches / quantized KV.

Papers & short notes (rapid skims)
1) Sparse-KV for long sequences (arXiv:2308.12345) — main takeaway: selective retention of prefix vectors based on attention salience.
  - Mechanism: periodically compress older KV pairs using PCA-like projection; keep top-k by salience.
  - Nice: reduces memory while preserving high-impact context.
  - Question: runtime overhead of compress/restore on GPU — can this be async on CPU?

2) Adaptive-batching heuristics (workshop slides from S. Gupta)
  - Idea: maintain two windows: fast-path low-latency queue (for SLO requests) and high-throughput batch window for background requests. Dynamically move clients between windows based on SLA labels.
  - Implementation thought: integrate with our routing policies so Dedicated pools can advertise 'low-latency tokens/second' budgets.

3) Quantized-kernel regressions (internal benchmark talk)
  - Observed: int8 quantization of KV tensors shows small drop in next-token accuracy but outsized latency/cost improvements on A100s and future HW.
  - We should instrument a quality metric (ROUGE/semantic-similarity) on a small prompt set to detect regressions per model-variant.

Mini-experiment sketches (fast to run)
- KV eviction policies A/B test (2 days): LRU vs salience-based vs time-decay on a curated dataset of chat sessions (10k). Measure rouge-l/embedding-sim of model continuations when earlier context is removed.
  - Data: anonymized interactive logs from product-sandbox (INF-2148) — need CS signoff.
  - Success metric: <3% drop in answer-sim but 30% reduction in KV memory.

- Async compression prototype (3 days): move simple PCA compress/decompress off the hot path using CUDA streams or async CPU copy. Evaluate end-to-end tail latency for 95/99th.

Notes on serving/runtime constraints
- Our runtime currently pins KV cache to CUDA memory per-GPU. That gives fastest ops but painful if per-tenant KV grows. Two options:
  1. Hybrid GPU/CPU pinned memory with fast DMA — less ideal for small latency SLOs.
  2. Sharded KV across multiple GPUs with cheap routing — adds inter-GPU comms; might break scaling assumptions.

Operational safety & fallback logic (rough)
- If cache hit rate falls below threshold for a customer (because eviction policy wrong or workload shift), route to a higher-capacity model variant that recomputes longer context but with higher cost (fallback billing apply).
- Implement 'soft-failure' mode: when async compression fails, continue serving cold (no cache) but flag diagnostics.

Eval design notes (how to measure "quality")
- Don't rely solely on perplexity. Make small human-curated prompt sets per vertical (summarization, code, retrieval-augmented Q/A). Compute:
  - embedding-sim of continuation vs golden continuation (cosine on sentence-transformer embed)
  - pass@k or exact-match where applicable (code, QA)
  - measure divergence as function of removed-KV proportion. Plot degradation curves.

Unresolved questions / decisions
- Should we prefer lossy compression (PCA/quantize) or smarter eviction (salience)? Both require ops work. Which yields better unit-cost? (Need small benchmark).
- Can we repurpose existing Optimize suggestions (redwood-optimize) to recommend per-customer KV configs based on traffic patterns? Feels plausible.
- SLA implications: if we add async compression, does it change our SLO calculation for tail latency? Need SRE input.

Action items (owners + tentative dates)
- Run KV eviction A/B (data access + scripts): Asha Patel — start 9/19, finish 9/23. JIRA: INF-2150.
- Prototype async compress/decompress: me (Eliot) — POC by 9/22, demo 9/23. Link: GH WIP PR referenced above.
- SRE sync: Luca Romano — schedule 30-min sync by 9/20 to validate tail-latency constraints and possible infra changes.
- CS/legal: request approval for anonymized logs for the A/B test — Asha to own.

Loose ideas that looked promising in hallway convos
- 'Prefix hinting': allow client to attach a tiny hint vector that tells the serving runtime which parts of KV are more likely to be used (cheap extra metadata per request). Could improve cache hit without moving big bytes.
- 'Micro-checkpointing' for long user sessions: periodically snapshot compressed KV to object storage, but keep a small delta on-GPU for immediate use. If we need the full history, we can stream-in incrementally.

Random quick code sketch (pseudocode)
- eviction decision: if (kv_size > soft_limit) { candidates = score_by_salience(kv); evict_lowest(candidates, amount); async_compress(evicted); }
- score_by_salience: last_attention_weight * position_decay * topic_relevance

Notes to self (reminders)
- Keep the prototype minimal: aim for measurable metrics, not perfect system.
- When writing RFC, include a cost model: bytes-in-GPU -> $/token saved tradeoff.

References & links (to copy into a nicer doc later)
- arXiv:2308.12345 — 'Selective KV retention for long-context' (note: placeholder id used in workshop slides)
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123 (async-compress sketch)
- CONFLUENCE-ENG-9876 (workshop notes)

End of dump. Will tidy up into an RFC if we can show promising numbers from A/B and the async POC.
